title: A bounded projective resolution is equivalent to vanishing of one Ext degree
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $X$ an $R$-module, and $n\ge0$ an integer. The following are equivalent: (1) $X$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], namely an exact sequence $0\to P_n\to\cdots\to P_0\to X\to0$ with all $P_i$ projective; (2) for every $R$-module $Y$, the group $\operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}_R(X,Y)$ [def-pc-ext] is zero. Equivalently, in (2) one may require $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(X,Y)=0$ for every $Y$ and every $i\ge n+1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext, line 26725), parts (1)--(3), tag verified in tags/tags

proof.text: First prove (1) implies (2) by induction on the bound $n$. At $n=0$, exactness of $0\to P_0\to X\to0$ makes $X$ isomorphic to the projective module $P_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension, def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]; projectivity is invariant under isomorphism by its lifting definition [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Then [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ext-criterion] gives $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(X,Y)=0$ for every $Y$ and every $i\ge1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext), proof of (1) implies (2), with the projective case from Lemma Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective)

proof.text: For the induction step, suppose (1) holds with bound $n+1$. In an exact resolution $0\to P_{n+1}\to\cdots\to P_1\to P_0\xrightarrow{q}X\to0$, put $K=\ker q$. Exactness [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] yields $0\to P_{n+1}\to\cdots\to P_1\to K\to0$, a projective resolution of $K$ of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. For every $Y$ and $i\ge n+2$, the induction hypothesis gives $\operatorname{Ext}^{i-1}_R(K,Y)=0$ since $i-1\ge n+1$. Also $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(P_0,Y)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ext-criterion]. The short exact sequence $0\to K\to P_0\to X\to0$ and [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-first-variable] give the exact segment $\operatorname{Ext}^{i-1}_R(K,Y)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_R(P_0,Y)$; its outer groups are zero, so the middle group is zero. This finishes (1) implies (2) for every $n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext), proof of (1) implies (2), using the long exact Ext sequence of Lemma Tag 065P (lemma-reverse-long-exact-seq-ext) for the induction step
Algebra, Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext), proof of (2) implies (3)

proof.text: Prove (3) implies (1) by induction on $n$. For $n=0$, the hypothesis says $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_R(X,Y)=0$ for all $Y$ [def-pc-ext]. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ext-criterion], $X$ is projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and its identity map gives the length-zero exact projective resolution $0\to X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext), proof of (3) implies (1), n = 0, invoking Lemma Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective)

proof.text: For the induction step from $n$ to $n+1$, let $F=\bigoplus_{x\in X}R$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and send its basis vector $e_x$ to $x$; this defines a surjection $q:F\twoheadrightarrow X$, since every $x$ is the image of $e_x$. It is projective by [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-projective]. Put $K=\ker q$. Assume $\operatorname{Ext}^{n+2}_R(X,Y)=0$ for every $Y$. The short exact sequence $0\to K\to F\xrightarrow{q}X\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] and [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-first-variable] give, for every $Y$, the exact segment $\operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}_R(F,Y)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}_R(K,Y)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{n+2}_R(X,Y)$. Its left group is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ext-criterion], because $n+1\ge1$; its right group is zero by hypothesis. Thus $\operatorname{Ext}^{n+1}_R(K,Y)=0$ for every $Y$. The induction hypothesis gives a projective resolution $0\to Q_n\to\cdots\to Q_0\to K\to0$. Compose $Q_0\to K$ with $K\hookrightarrow F$ and append $F\xrightarrow{q}X$: $0\to Q_n\to\cdots\to Q_0\to F\to X\to0$ is exact at $Q_0$ because $K\hookrightarrow F$ is injective, and at $F$ because $\operatorname{im}(Q_0\to F)=K=\ker q$; all its terms are projective. Hence it is a projective resolution of $X$ of length $\le n+1$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. This completes (3) implies (1).
